title: Huawei and Sungrow top Wood Mackenzie's global inverter ranking
lede: Wood Mackenzie's H1 2025 ranking scores inverter makers on service, R&D, supply chain and ESG, not only on how many units they ship. Huawei (93.9) and Sungrow (93.7) finished almost level at the top, followed by SMA, Fronius, Ginlong/Solis and GoodWe.
bullets: Top 10: Huawei, Sungrow, SMA, Fronius, Ginlong/Solis, GoodWe, TMEIC, SolarEdge, Aiswei/Solplanet and Enphase; together they hold about 71% of the global market.
23 manufacturers from seven countries were assessed, covering about 90% of global inverter shipments in 2024.
Score weights: ESG/CSR 30%, after-sales service 15%, R&D 15%, supply chain stability 15%, capacity utilisation 10%, certifications, financial condition and manufacturing experience 5% each.
All top-10 makers are rated Grade A and now offer warranty extensions of 20 years or more, to match the working life of solar panels.
Wood Mackenzie expects global inverter shipments to dip about 2% in 2025 (577 GWac) and about 9% in 2026 (523 GWac) before recovering.
thailand_note: The ranking is not a sales chart. For a Thai owner, what matters is the service a brand gives in Thailand, from a local hotline to replacement units: ask who handles a warranty claim here and how fast a replacement arrives. Several top-10 brands, including Huawei, Solis and GoodWe, are widely installed in Thailand.
